setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "calendar-creator-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for calendar-creator skill evals"

evals.name: day-view-with-card-events
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: build a calendar eval_dock_schedule_calendar that shows one day of dock appointments with one column per dock door. Doors come from a datasource you create (ds_eval_dock_doors), appointments from a second datasource (ds_eval_dock_appointments_by_day) that takes the start and end of the selected day. Each appointment tile must show its lookup code and carrier, so create the event card eval_dock_appointment_card for that. Add a date filter plus Previous / Today / Next buttons.
evals.expected_output: A validated and upserted calendar (cti 12, type day) whose events render through the newly created card, whose events datasource receives a day window derived from the date filter, and whose navigation buttons move the date and re-derive the window.
expectations: A calendar body is created with configurationTypeId 12, type "day", and referenceName eval_dock_schedule_calendar (ends in _calendar)
The calendar title is a sentence-case display name that is not byte-identical to the referenceName
dayViewConfig.eventsConfig.eventContentType is "card" and eventContentConfig.configId is eval_dock_appointment_card with moduleId set to the card's package
The card (configurationTypeId 11) is upserted on the branch before the calendar that references it
eventContentConfig.configParameters contain one entry per card inParam, bound with $calendarEvent.entity.<field> expressions
columnsConfig.text and matchEventToColumn reference $column; eventsConfig start/end/title reference $calendarEvent
The events datasource receives the day window either from declared $calendar.vars (set in a date-change flow) or from an expression over the view_date filter
The Previous/Next flows shift the date filter with $utils.date.add(-1/1, 'day', ...) and re-derive the window (calling the date-change flow as $calendar.<flow>() and/or $calendar.refresh())
nextPageText, previousPageText and currentPageInfoText are TS-quoted string literals (e.g. "'Next doors'"), not bare words
Each datasourceConfig carries datasourceKeyDef, a configParameters entry for every datasource inParam, and the datasource's full configOutParameters
The calendar's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate calendar' run before 'dxs configuration upsert calendar'

evals.name: hour-segment-click-flow
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: on an existing day-view calendar eval_line_schedule_calendar (create a minimal one first if it does not exist), make clicking an empty time slot open a form eval_new_booking_form (create it) pre-filled with the clicked column's id and the clicked start time, and refresh the calendar if the user confirms.
evals.expected_output: The calendar's hour-segment click handler is a full inline cti-9 flow under dayViewConfig.hourSegmentClickedFlow with hasHourSegmentClickedFlow true, reading $event.date and $event.column, opening the form dialog and refreshing on confirm.
expectations: dayViewConfig.hasHourSegmentClickedFlow is true
dayViewConfig.hourSegmentClickedFlow is a full inline flow object (configurationTypeId 9 with nodes[0].stepConfig.executeCodeConfig.code) — NOT a { flowId } reference and NOT null
The click-flow code reads $event.date and $event.column (e.g. $event.column.Id) and does not read $event.calendarEvent
The form is opened through the generated $shell.<Package>.open<referenceName>Dialog method with snake_case preserved (openeval_new_booking_formDialog)
The calendar calls $calendar.refresh() after a confirmed dialog result
Any edit to an existing calendar extracts the inner body (jq .json) from the get envelope before editing
The calendar's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate calendar' run before 'dxs configuration upsert calendar'

evals.name: drag-drop-reschedule
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create eval_work_order_calendar where dragging an order to another slot or column reschedules it — keep the original duration, move the start to the drop time, and move it to the dropped column. Also add an unassigned side list; dropping an order there clears its column. Persist through a function, not an action.
evals.expected_output: A calendar with hasHourSegmentEventDroppedFlow and hasUnscheduledEvents/hasUnscheduledEventDroppedFlow true, each paired with a full inline flow; the drop flow computes the new end from the preserved duration, writes via a function, and refreshes.
expectations: dayViewConfig.hasHourSegmentEventDroppedFlow is true and hourSegmentEventDroppedFlow is a full inline cti-9 flow object (not null, not a { flowId } reference)
The drop flow reads $event.calendarEvent.entity, $event.date and $event.column.Id
The drop flow preserves duration (computes the original end-minus-start and adds it to $event.date, e.g. via $utils.date.add)

hasUnscheduledEvents is true and unscheduledEventsConfig is populated with pageSize, datasourceConfig, a TS-quoted title (e.g. "'Unassigned'"), hasUnscheduledEventDroppedFlow true and an inline unscheduledEventDroppedFlow
The unscheduled-drop flow reads $event.calendarEvent and does not reference $event.column
Persistence goes through $flows.<Package>.<function> (no action call from the calendar), followed by $calendar.refresh()
No has<X>Flow flag is false while its sibling flow is populated, and none is true while its sibling is null
The response flags drag/drop persistence and revert behaviour as needing a Preview check rather than claiming it verified
The calendar's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate calendar' run before 'dxs configuration upsert calendar'

evals.name: naming-title-and-view-type
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: we need a weekly production calendar. Name the component ProductionWeek and title it the same. Show production orders per line.
evals.expected_output: The skill explains that only the day view is authorable (week deserializes but fails codegen), proposes a day-view calendar with Previous/Next navigation, renames the component to a snake_case _calendar referenceName with a distinct sentence-case title, and validates before upsert.
expectations: type is "day" in the authored body — the response states that week/month are not authorable (validate fails with Cannot find name 'ICalendarEvent' or equivalent) rather than silently authoring type "week"
The referenceName is snake_case and ends in _calendar (e.g. production_week_calendar), not ProductionWeek
The title is a sentence-case display name distinct from the referenceName (e.g. 'Production schedule'), not byte-identical to it
configurationTypeId is 12
Events render through a card (eventContentType "card")
The calendar's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate calendar' run before 'dxs configuration upsert calendar'
